model: Underlying profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route), with blended exit P/E and exit P/B terminal

inputs.sbc_source: None: no share option scheme, share award scheme or share-based payment expense appears in the FY2025 annual report or H1 FY2026 interim report (grep of both filings). SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime, Friday regular-session close; HKEX shut over the weekend)
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,841m basic shares in issue (unchanged since the 2019 bonus issue; no buybacks FY2017-FY2025). The HK$8bn 0.5% convertible bond due 2030 (conversion price adjusted to HK$35.35, ~226-232m shares; IAS 33 diluted count 5,073m at H1 FY2026) is out of the money at the current price and is treated as debt: its interest accretion is already inside underlying profit, so adding the conversion shares as well would charge it twice. Held flat; no SBC dilution to model.
inputs.stream_basis: The capitalised stream is underlying profit attributable to equity shareholders (company definition: reported attributable profit excluding the after-tax fair-value change on investment properties held by subsidiaries, associates and JVs). It is post-interest (including the HK$2.1bn/yr paid to the controlling family's finance company), post-tax, post-NCI and includes Henderson's share of associates (HK&China Gas 41.53%, HK Ferry, Sunlight REIT) and JVs. It is therefore capitalised at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero; deducting net debt afterwards would charge the debt twice. Payout check: FY2025 dividends HK$8.7bn paid vs underlying HK$6.1bn; FY2020-24 dividends HK$8.7bn/yr vs underlying HK$9.6-14.9bn; shareholders' equity flat at HK$320-335bn for eight years, so the stream has in practice been distributed, not retained, which is what discounting it in full assumes. The engine fields are used as follows: revenue = underlying profit, EBITDA margin 100%, SBC/D&A/capex/tax/working capital 0.
inputs.fy0_stream_history: Underlying profit HK$m: FY2019 ~14,620 (EPS 3.02), FY2020 14,899, FY2021 13,624, FY2022 9,629, FY2023 9,706, FY2024 9,774, FY2025 6,063, H1 FY2025 3,048, H1 FY2026 5,071 (FY2025 AR five-year summary line 4389/3798; H1 FY2026 interim highlights). Reported FCF FY2025 HK$8,603m (OCF 12,325 less capex 3,722); FY2017 and FY2021 cash FCF distorted by land purchases (FY2021 HK$54.9bn incl. the New Central Harbourfront Site 3 / Central Yards site).
inputs.balance_sheet_memo: H1 FY2026 (30 Jun 2026): bank loans 60,017, guaranteed notes 8,894, convertible bond debt component 7,210, amounts due to related companies 3,788 -> company 'total debt' 79,909; cash and bank balances 21,477; company net debt 58,432 (17.9% of equity). PLUS amount due to a fellow subsidiary 76,955 (FY2025: 80,618) -> economic net debt 135,387, 41.6% of shareholders' equity of 325,555. Interest in associates carried at 51,948; HK&China Gas stake carried at 42,222 vs market value 54,318 at 31 Dec 2025 (AR note 20).
inputs.fellow_subsidiary_loan_treatment: TREATED AS DEBT, not equity-like funding. The HK$76.96bn (H1 FY2026) 'amount due to a fellow subsidiary' is owed to Henderson Finance Company Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Henderson Development Limited (the Lee family's private holdco). Per FY2025 AR note 33, the connected-transaction disclosure and the interest-rate risk table, it is unsecured, INTEREST-BEARING (HIBOR-referenced or fixed: 67,534 floating + 13,084 fixed at FY2025), not expected to be settled within a year and has no fixed repayment terms. It cost HK$2,113m of interest in FY2025 (HK$2,877m in FY2024; note 42(a)). It carries no residual claim, no conversion right and no subordination: a minority holder ranks behind it exactly as behind a bank loan, and the family can call it at will. The company's headline net-debt and 17.9% gearing figures exclude it; on an economic basis gearing is ~41.6%. It grew from HK$4.4bn (FY2020) to HK$80.6bn (FY2025), principally funding the HK$50.8bn Central Yards site (FY2021) and dividends in excess of underlying profit. In THIS model the loan is charged once, through its interest inside underlying profit, and it is already netted in book NAV for the P/B cross-check. Had an EV-based owner-FCF DCF been used it would have had to be added to net debt (~HK$15.9/share).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in HKD (the flows' currency; HKD is pegged to USD): risk-free ~4.0% (US 10-year ~4.1%, HK Exchange Fund Notes 10-year ~3.6-3.9%), ERP 5.5%, levered beta ~1.0 on economic gearing of ~42% (headline beta on 17.9% gearing ~0.85-0.9 understates it) -> 9.5%. Same rate in all three scenarios; downside is carried in the bear scenario and its 25% weight, not a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial (lease liabilities HK$764m at H1 FY2026); the lease charge is inside underlying profit and lease liabilities are not deducted again.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stream is attributable-only (underlying profit attributable to equity shareholders; NCI of HK$17.8bn mainly Miramar/Henderson Investment minorities excluded) so NCI is charged once and no bridge deduction is made.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Henderson Land is a Hong Kong developer/investor holdco (property development ~70% of revenue, HK$8.7bn gross rental, plus 41.53% of HK&China Gas and other listed stakes). Routing per dcf-methods SKILL.md: it straddles 'inventory-heavy developer' (blended NTA exit-P/B and earnings exit-P/E) and 'holdco / compounder-of-book'. A plain owner-FCF DCF is wrong here: consolidated cash FCF excludes associate/JV earnings (Towngas, mainland JVs) except as dividends, swings with land purchases (FY2021 -HK$54bn) and pre-sale timing, and an EV-to-equity bridge would require valuing ~HK$135bn of economic net debt against a cash flow that does not include the assets it funds. A pure book-NAV model is also wrong: book NAV of HK$67.25/share has not compounded in eight years (equity CAGR -0.3%), underlying ROE is 2-3%, and the controlling family has never realised NAV; HK developers have traded at 0.3-0.6x book for a decade. Chosen: capitalise underlying attributable profit at the cost of equity over 10 years, with the terminal multiple set as a 50/50 blend of an exit P/E and an exit P/B on a flat ~HK$330bn book (base 12x P/E and 0.45x P/B -> 13x; bull 14x P/E and 0.55x P/B -> ~14x after Gordon check; bear 10x P/E and 0.30x P/B -> 10x). That implements the routing table's developer row on the engine route. NAV CROSS-CHECK: book NAV/share HK$67.25 at 30 Jun 2026; marking the HK&China Gas stake to market adds ~HK$2.5/share (54,318 vs 42,222 carrying); the ~38.4m sq ft New Territories farmland bank at historical cost is the main unbooked upside and is why the bull exit P/B is 0.55x. CURRENT PRICE = 0.40x book and ~14.5x the FY2026 underlying profit estimate. Interest income is NOT stripped: the stream is post-net-interest and cash is not added back. Buybacks: none ever; flat count is the company's actual record, not a modelling convention. Dividend: FY2025 cut 30% to HK$1.26; H1 FY2026 interim HK$0.50 (flat). HIBOR sensitivity: ~84% of the fellow-subsidiary loan and ~75% of bank loans float; +100bp HIBOR is ~HK$1.1-1.3bn pre-tax, ~HK$0.2/share or ~11% of base-case underlying EPS.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.3%) diverges sharply from EPS CAGR (-11% to -15%) and from cash FCF CAGR (+13.8% 5yr, off a FY2020 low). Book is held flat by full payout and investment-property fair-value losses; EPS fell with the HK residential and mainland downturn. Neither is a forward growth rate; the forward path is a recovery from the FY2025 trough (underlying EPS 1.25) toward the FY2022-24 run-rate (~2.0), not a compounding rate.
historical_growth.notes: No SBC and no interest-income adjustment applies (SBC-zero; the company is a net borrower), so owner FCF = reported FCF. FY2017 and FY2021 cash FCF are dominated by land purchases and are excluded from judgment. Reported EPS includes investment-property fair-value changes; underlying EPS is the cleaner series and fell from HK$3.08 (FY2020) to HK$1.25 (FY2025) before recovering to HK$1.05 in H1 FY2026 alone.

base.narrative: Underlying profit HK$9.0bn in FY2026 (H1 HK$5.07bn incl. a NT land-resumption gain; ~HK$6.9bn of contracted sales due for H2 recognition), HK$9.3bn FY2027, HK$9.7bn FY2028 and HK$10.0bn FY2029 as Central Yards Phase 1 (70% pre-let) and The Henderson add rent, then 2% nominal growth. That is a return to the FY2022-24 run-rate of ~HK$2.0/share, not to the FY2019-21 HK$3.0.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 50/50 blend of 12x exit P/E (HK developer mid-cycle) and 0.45x exit P/B on ~HK$330bn book (=~HK$148bn, ~13.2x FY2035 stream) -> 13x. Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% is 13.6x, so the cap binds.

bull.narrative: HK residential upcycle (sell-side +10-15% 2026 price forecasts) sustained through the eight H2-2026 launches and the urban-redevelopment pipeline; continued NT farmland conversion/resumption gains under the Northern Metropolis; Central Yards fully let; mainland leasing stabilises; HIBOR stays low. Underlying profit HK$9.5bn / 11.0bn / 12.0bn / 12.5bn (EPS ~2.6 by FY2029, still below FY2019-20), then 3%.
bull.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: Blend of 14x exit P/E and 0.55x exit P/B (crediting part of the unbooked NT land bank). Gordon at 9.5%/3.0% is 15.8x; cap binds at 14x.

bear.narrative: FY2026 at HK$8.2bn flattered by the one-off land-resumption gain, then back to the FY2025 trough of ~HK$6.5bn and flat: the HK residential rebound stalls after 2026, mainland development losses widen and mainland rents keep falling, HIBOR rises on the ~HK$135bn economic net debt (84% of the family loan floats), and the controlling family keeps funding dividends with related-party debt rather than earnings. 1% growth thereafter.
bear.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 10x exit P/E, consistent with a ~0.22x exit P/B on ~HK$330bn book (below the 0.30x trough of HK peers, so the P/E side is the binding constraint). Gordon at 9.5%/1.0% is 11.9x; cap binds.

scenario_narratives.base: Henderson's earnings recover from the FY2025 trough (underlying EPS HK$1.25) to roughly the FY2022-24 level (~HK$1.9-2.1) on the H1 FY2026 sales rebound (HK contracted sales +188%, HK$17.1bn unrecognised) and new Central rental assets (The Henderson, Central Yards Phase 1 70% pre-let), offset by mainland drag and ~HK$4.4bn/yr gross interest on bank and related-party debt. The market continues to price HK developers on earnings, not NAV: exit at 12x P/E / 0.45x book.
scenario_narratives.bull: A durable HK housing upcycle plus Northern Metropolis monetisation of the 38.4m sq ft NT farmland bank, Central Yards fully let and lower HIBOR lift underlying EPS toward HK$2.6 by FY2029, and the NAV discount narrows to ~0.55x book.
scenario_narratives.bear: The H1 FY2026 rebound proves a one-off (it included a land-resumption gain), earnings settle back at the FY2025 level and stay there as mainland losses, mainland rental oversupply and higher HIBOR on ~84%-floating related-party borrowings bite; the family-controlled structure keeps the stock at a 10x P/E and a ~0.2-0.3x book multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: underlying profit has fallen in five of the last six years, H1 FY2026 included a non-recurring resumption gain, and economic gearing is ~42% once the controlling family's HK$77bn floating-rate loan is counted. Base 50%: the H2 FY2026 recognition pipeline (HK$6.9bn) is contracted. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs a sustained HK housing upcycle, NT land monetisation and a narrower NAV discount simultaneously.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value what a minority shareholder actually receives: an underlying-profit stream that has been fully paid out for eight years, capitalised at a 9.5% HKD cost of equity, with the exit set by how HK developers are actually priced (P/E and a deep discount to book), not by book NAV that the controlling family has never realised. Book NAV (HK$67.25) is the ceiling reference, not the estimate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Related-party funding: the HK$77bn amount due to a fellow subsidiary is interest-bearing, has no fixed repayment terms and is at the controlling family's discretion; it is treated as debt and charged through interest. Reclassifying it as equity-like would overstate value.
HIBOR: ~84% of the family loan and ~75% of bank loans float; +100bp is ~11% of base-case underlying EPS.
Sales timing: development profit is recognised on handover, so single years swing by 50%+ (FY2024 HK$5.6bn vs FY2025 HK$1.3bn pre-tax development contribution).
Mainland China development losses and rental oversupply (H1 FY2026 mainland contracted sales -74%).

Upside not in the base: the ~38.4m sq ft NT farmland bank at historical cost and the ~HK$12bn mark-to-market gain on the HK&China Gas stake; a privatisation by the controlling family at a NAV discount narrower than today's 0.40x would also crystallise value.
Convertible bond (conversion HK$35.35) dilutes ~4.6% only if the share price passes the bull-case value.
